criterionOutcomes.criterion: When Call samples are returned, the timeline chart shows call state, service technology, and signal strength across the test duration.
criterionOutcomes.reason: Focused live check on 2 November: the built-in expanded Call analysis view for 5 October 2026, 19:35:02 displays Call initiated (CI), Connected (CC) and Call ended (CE) annotations over the signal-strength timeline spanning the 70-second test. The readable returned samples show Idle, Off Hook and Connected transitions; the chart marks initiation, connection and end. The source asks for call state over time, without prescribing a separate continuous state series or lane. The prior Unverified interpretation imposed that extra presentation requirement. Service technology is shown as Service in the same analysis view, accepted by the user. This is a source-aligned reassessment with a fresh chart capture, not a new full attempt.

coverageChecks.assertion: Timeline displays call-state transitions across the returned test
coverageChecks.reason: Visible CI, CC and CE chart annotations across the duration satisfy the source without inventing a separate state-series requirement.

criterionOutcomes.criterion: While Call details are loading, the dialog shows the standard loading state; when details are unavailable, it shows the standard no-data state; when loading fails, it shows the standard error state, with no incorrect Call data displayed.
criterionOutcomes.reason: The existing disclosed delayed-request and HTTP 503 checks establish loading/error handling. A new genuine no-data fixture now completes the unavailable-analysis branch: after displaying a populated Call, normal selection of zero-duration Call 132762259 shows No data available, retains only its correct summary and clears the earlier chart/sample table. This proves the actual no-analysis case, not arbitrary missing-record or backend-error schemas. New fixture check was not simulated; the older loading/error checks remain explicitly simulated.
